candidate_relations.reason: The MRI finding of a pedunculated bony protrusion arising from the posterolateral plantar calcaneus with no plantar fascia thickening or signal alteration is more consistent with an osteochondroma (cartilage-capped exostosis) than an enthesophyte. An enthesophyte arises at a tendon/ligament insertion due to traction and is typically located at the plantar fascia origin on the medial calcaneal tubercle, not the posterolateral plantar calcaneus. The candidate asserts a different etiology and anatomical subtype incompatible with the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Plantar calcaneal enthesophyte is a traction/degenerative spur at the plantar fascia insertion, distinct from osteochondroma which is a cartilage-capped benign bone tumor; both are pedunculated bony protrusions but represent different pathological entities

case_quality_flags: Posterolateral plantar calcaneal location and MRI characteristics strongly favor osteochondroma over enthesophyte; the distinction is clinically and pathologically significant
